## Overview

**CSIDH** (Commutative Supersingular Isogeny Diffie-Hellman) is a post-quantum key exchange protocol proposed by Castryck et al. [@csidh]. It serves as an isogeny-based analogue to traditional Diffie-Hellman key exchange, built on the framework of Couveignes, Rostovtsev, and Stolbunov (CRS).

Because CSIDH provides a truly commutative group action, it is highly versatile and serves as the mathematical foundation for more advanced primitives, such as the isogeny-based signature scheme [CSI-FiSh](../digital-signature/csi-fish.qmd).

Unlike SIDH (which uses non-commutative endomorphism rings), CSIDH leverages a **commutative group action** by restricting to supersingular elliptic curves defined over a prime field $\mathbb{F}_p$ whose endomorphism rings are isomorphic to an order in an imaginary quadratic field.

---

## Mathematical Foundation {#sec-math-foundation}

Let $p$ be a prime of the form $p = 4 \cdot \ell_1 \cdot \ell_2 \cdots \ell_n - 1$, where $\ell_i$ are small, distinct odd primes. 

### The Curve Space
We consider the set $\mathcal{S}_R$ of $\mathbb{F}_p$-isomorphism classes of supersingular elliptic curves $E/\mathbb{F}_p$ whose $\mathbb{F}_p$-endomorphism ring $\text{End}_{\mathbb{F}_p}(E)$ is exactly the order $R = \mathbb{Z}[\pi]$, where $\pi$ is the Frobenius endomorphism satisfying $\pi^2 = -p$. These curves can be written in Montgomery form:

$$E_A: y^2 = x^3 + Ax^2 + x$$

### The Class Group Action

The ideal class group $\text{Cl}(R)$ acts freely and transitively on the set $\mathcal{S}_R$. Given an ideal class $[\mathfrak{a}] \in \text{Cl}(R)$ and a curve class $[E] \in \mathcal{S}_R$, the group action is defined via the idealisogeny:

$$[\mathfrak{a}] * E = E / E[\mathfrak{a}]$$

Where $E[\mathfrak{a}]$ is the intersection of the kernels of all endomorphisms in $\mathfrak{a}$. Because $\text{Cl}(R)$ is an abelian group, the action commutes:

$$[\mathfrak{a}] * ([\mathfrak{b}] * E) = ([\mathfrak{a}\mathfrak{b}]) * E = [\mathfrak{b}] * ([\mathfrak{a}] * E)$$

---

## Key Exchange Protocol

The commutativity of the group action allows a direct translation of the classical Diffie-Hellman matrix or exponentiation paradigm.

| Alice | Public | Bob |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| Chooses secret ideal $[\mathfrak{a}]$ | | Chooses secret ideal $[\mathfrak{b}]$ |
| Computes $E_A = [\mathfrak{a}] * E_0$ | $\xrightarrow{\quad E_A \quad}$ | |
| | $\xleftarrow{\quad E_B \quad}$ | Computes $E_B = [\mathfrak{b}] * E_0$ |
| Computes $E_{BA} = [\mathfrak{a}] * E_B$ | | Computes $E_{AB} = [\mathfrak{b}] * E_A$ |

> **Shared Secret:** Since the group action commutes, $E_{BA} = E_{AB}$. The Montgomery coefficient $A \in \mathbb{F}_p$ of this final curve serves as the shared cryptographic secret.

```{.tikz}
\usetikzlibrary{arrows.meta}
\begin{tikzpicture}

  \node (E0)  at (3, 4)  {$E_0$};
  \node (EA)  at (0, 2)  {$E_A = [\mathfrak{a}] * E_0$};
  \node (EB)  at (6, 2)  {$E_B = [\mathfrak{b}] * E_0$};
  \node (EAB) at (3, 0)  {$E_{AB} = E_{BA}$};

  \draw[-{Stealth}, thick] (E0)  -- node[left,  midway] {$[\mathfrak{a}]$} (EA);
  \draw[-{Stealth}, thick] (E0)  -- node[right, midway] {$[\mathfrak{b}]$} (EB);
  \draw[-{Stealth}, thick] (EA)  -- node[right, midway] {$[\mathfrak{b}]$} (EAB);
  \draw[-{Stealth}, thick] (EB)  -- node[left,  midway] {$[\mathfrak{a}]$} (EAB);

\end{tikzpicture}
```

$$
E_{AB}
=
[\mathfrak b] * E_A
=
[\mathfrak b] * ([\mathfrak a] * E_0)
=
[\mathfrak a] * ([\mathfrak b] * E_0)
=
[\mathfrak a] * E_B
=
E_{BA}.
$$

---

## Performance and Parameter Sets

CSIDH parameters are evaluated by their quantum security levels (NIST categories) against advanced sieve algorithms like Kuperberg's hidden shift algorithm.

| Parameter Set | Prime Bits ($\log_2 p$) | Public Key Size | Key Exchange Speed |
|---|---|---|---|
| **CSIDH-512** | 511 bits | 64 Bytes | ~30-100 ms |
| **CSIDH-1024** | 1024 bits | 128 Bytes | ~200-500 ms |
